title: Investigate late-attribution and token skew caused by out-of-order streaming fragments
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Multiple customers have reported brief overcharges and incorrect per-session token tallies for long-lived streaming sessions when clients intermittently reconnect or send fragments out of order. Our current metering pipeline assumes monotonic fragment offsets and a single canonical finalization event; real-world clients and proxies can violate both assumptions. This ticket scopes investigation and fixes covering: 1) deterministic attribution of input tokens when fragments arrive out of order or are replayed, 2) reconciling partial output credits if the finalization/terminal frame is delayed or duplicated, 3) ensuring idempotent checkpointing and ledger writes under concurrent rewrite scenarios. Goals: - Produce a reproducible test harness that can simulate out-of-order frames, partial reconnects, and duplicated terminal frames. - Propose a small set of protocol-level invariants (+compatibility shim) that let the metering reconciler make safe, bounded decisions without requiring client changes. - Implement fixes in reconciler and persistence layers with minimal latency impact and add e2e assertions for billing correctness. - Run canary on dedicated lab accounts and prepare migration/fallback plan for older clients. Non-goals: full client SDK changes (will be addressed with follow-up), redesign of billing model.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Ava Martinez: Filed after incident INC-2026-02-stream-billing; initial triage shows ~1.8% overcharge on some long-lived sessions. Added dependencies to ENG-314271 (sparse-chunkization) and ENG-271888 (http/ws transcoding).

2026-02-14 - Ravi Patel: Reproduced issue locally by creating a harness that reorders frames and simulates TCP-level reconnects. Found three root causes: duplicate terminal frame processing, session snapshot race in ledger writer, and tokenizer length drift between client-side and server-side heuristics. Will focus remediation on ledger idempotency and a conservative terminal-frame dedupe window first.

2026-02-20 - Lena Chen (Reviewer): Reviewed proposed ledger change. Concern: changing write semantics could increase IOPS on accounting DB. Trade-off suggested: use a lightweight dedupe index with TTL per session to avoid full rewrite. Also suggested adding a vector clock per session to fast-fail stale writes.

2026-02-24 - Ravi Patel: Implemented prototype dedupe index (in-memory LRU cache backed by Redis) and vector-clock metadata. Benchmarked impact: 3% p99 latency increase for write path in our lab but reduces reclaims and double-credits by >99% for simulated duplicates. Push PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8642

2026-03-01 - QA: Added scenario list for e2e harness. Tests added: (A) out-of-order frames with single reconnect, (B) duplicated terminal frame, (C) lost terminal frame then delayed finalize, (D) tokenizer drift simulation with different tokenizers. Harness runs against staging runtime-1.24. Results: all tests passed except (D) which showed 2-token discrepancy under legacy tokenizer mode.

2026-03-05 - Product (Ishaan Rao): Customer communications drafted. Need a clear statement for customers affected and a recommended mitigation (short-term: bounded client retry backoff; long-term: we will deploy reconciler fix and provide SDK patch).

2026-03-09 - Security (K. Alvarez): Reviewed dedupe cache design. No encryption changes required but recommended we ensure audit logs contain dedupe decisions for downstream billing disputes. Added task to persist dedupe decision metadata to audit stream.

2026-03-12 - Ravi Patel: Merged reconciler persistence fix to canary. Canary plan: 10% of traffic from lab accounts + 3 pilot customers. Monitoring dashboards: metering.discrepancy.rate, ledger.write_errors, dedupe.cache.hit_rate. Early canary results (24h): discrepancy rate dropped from 1.8% to 0.03%. Scheduling follow-up to harden tokenizer drift handling.
